title: Pneumonia example
note: A 54-year-old synthetic patient presented with fever, productive cough, fatigue and shortness of breath for three days. Temperature was 38.4 C. Chest X-ray showed a right lower-lobe infiltrate. The assessment was community-acquired pneumonia. The patient was started on oral antibiotics, fluids and rest. Symptoms improved over the next several days. Follow-up with primary care was advised if symptoms worsened or failed to improve.

title: Hypertension follow-up
note: A 61-year-old synthetic patient attended a routine follow-up for hypertension. Home blood pressure readings remained above goal. The patient denied chest pain, fainting or shortness of breath. Medication adherence and low-sodium diet were reviewed. The clinician adjusted the antihypertensive regimen and requested repeat blood-pressure checks with follow-up in four weeks.

title: Diabetes review
note: A 47-year-old synthetic patient with type 2 diabetes attended a review visit. Recent glucose readings were elevated. The patient reported inconsistent meal planning but no symptoms of severe hypoglycemia. Lifestyle counseling, medication adherence and regular glucose monitoring were discussed. Laboratory testing was ordered and follow-up was planned.
